Verified against the toolchain source rather than taking the report on assertion: Go'"'"'s `os.Stat` on Windows derives a regular file'"'"'s permission bits from the read-only attribute alone — `0o444` when `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY` is set, `0o666` otherwise, with `0o111` added only for a directory (go1.26 `os/types_windows.go`, `fileStat.mode`). tool_input.message:
Your Windows exec-bit fix is pushed — I verified the gate myself (28 ok, 0 FAIL, all five targets exit 0) and replied to and resolved the Bugbot thread. The test earning its keep by asserting *which side* of the #12 split each Windows case lands in was the right call; it proves the branch is reachable again rather than just that the wrong FAIL is gone.

Two new Copilot findings on the same PR. I verified both against source before sending. Both are small and both are this branch's own defect class — prose that doesn't match code.

**1. `internal/doctor/sandbox.go:419-448` — a doc comment attached to the wrong function.** The comment block above `removeSandbox` is one contiguous block that *starts* with `shQuote`'s description ("shQuote wraps s in single quotes…") and runs straight into `removeSandbox`'s. Go therefore attaches the whole thing to `removeSandbox`, so `removeSandbox`'s doc opens by describing a different function, and `shQuote` at line 448 has no doc comment at all. Copilot's "also appears on line 446" is the same defect seen from the orphaned-function end, not a second instance.

Split it: `removeSandbox`'s comment describes only `removeSandbox`, and `shQuote` gets its own comment directly above it. Keep both texts — the content is fine, only the placement is wrong. While you're there, check whether any other function in the files this branch touched has the same run-together-comment problem; if the pattern repeats, fix every instance rather than just this one.

**2. `docs/design-hook-drift-detection.md:45-54` — the paragraph contradicts itself.** It still asserts in the present tense that "doctor checks only the seal (pre-commit) hook today" and that `CheckSealHook` "has no counterpart for the commit-msg/trailer hook at all", then closes with "Built: `CheckTrailerHook` … See DES-077." A reader cannot tell whether `ethos-hy40` is still pending or already closed.

This file is outside your original write-set, but it is in scope: this branch already modified it in `9853f7c`, and leaving a self-contradicting status paragraph in a doc we edited is not acceptable. Rewrite the lead-in to describe the post-DES-077 state — what the gap *was*, that `CheckTrailerHook` now closes it, and what remains true. Check the `ethos-kcbv` paragraph immediately below it for the same staleness, since that bead also landed in this branch and the stop-loss language may now be describing history as if it were pending.

Same bar as before: `make check` green with race, both counts reported, all five targets at exit 0. These are comment and prose changes so there is likely nothing to falsify — say so explicitly rather than inventing a test. Do not push; report and I push.
